Bratton has argued that celebrity behavior often drives the market for paparazzi photos, saying many stars cultivate attention, frequent paparazzi-heavy locations or otherwise participate in the publicity cycle. In his view, the issue is not simply photographers chasing unwilling subjects, but a celebrity culture in which fame, access and tabloid exposure are often mutually reinforcing.

Bratton has also suggested that when celebrities avoid the scene or stop feeding the spectacle, the frenzy tends to diminish. His position puts him at odds with those who say the city needs clearer restrictions on photographers’ conduct, but it reflects a broader debate over whether Los Angeles should regulate paparazzi more aggressively or whether the demand for celebrity images must be addressed at its source.
